items.description: The capital city of the Selangor state, known for the iconic Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque with its massive blue dome.
The administrative capital of Pahang state, situated near the mouth of the Kuantan River and famous for its nearby beaches.
A coastal city serving as the capital of Terengganu, renowned for its traditional Malay culture and the unique Crystal Mosque.
The capital of Kedah, known for the prominent Alor Setar Tower and as the birthplace of two Malaysian Prime Ministers.
Malaysia's administrative centre, characterized by elaborate Islamic architecture, large parks, and the famous Putra Mosque.
A prominent city in the Klang Valley, functioning as a major residential and commercial hub within the metropolitan area of Kuala Lumpur.
Initially a satellite township for Kuala Lumpur, it has evolved into a major self-contained city known for its diverse business districts.
A coastal city in Sarawak, historically significant as the birthplace of the Malaysian oil and gas industry after oil was discovered in 1910.
The largest city in Kedah, known for its rapid industrial development and proximity to the Bujang Valley historical site.
A coastal town in Johor, famous for its textile industry and vibrant local food scene centered around historical landmarks.
Located in Sabah, this town serves as a vital point for the surrounding agricultural industry and access to the Danum Valley conservation area.
One of the world's oldest tropical rainforests, estimated to be over 130 million years old and home to diverse wildlife.
A large public garden in Kuala Lumpur featuring a wide variety of tropical plants, lake views, and a dedicated orchid garden.
The national zoo of Malaysia, located in Hulu Kelang, housing thousands of animals from hundreds of different species.
